title: Operational Risk Identification, Mitigation and Reporting

maps.tested: Both sheets route these to crash-course notes rather than full reading, but flag best practices and the control taxonomy.
maps.specifics: The control sibling set (preventive, detective, corrective, directive) is a named GARP corruption operator and is worth securing even though the readings are deprioritised. RCSA, KRIs and loss-data collection are the identification and assessment tools.

vardeezReading: ORR-3, ORR-4, ORR-5 and ORR-6 are all untiered: "use crash course notes for ORR-1 to ORR-9; no Schweser needed."

selectors.name: Control types, key controls, automation, testing
selectors.what: Classifying a control as preventive (reduces likelihood, acts on causes), detective (alerts and limits impact; preventive if it detects a cause), corrective (lessens impact, not likelihood: back-ups, continuity plans) or directive (policies, procedures, training); also key versus non-key controls, the risks of automation, weak control designs and the four tests (inquiry, examination, observation, reperformance).

selectors.name: RCSA, scales and heatmap
selectors.what: Risk and control self-assessment: inherent versus residual risk, likelihood and impact scales (a 1-in-10-year event is a 10% chance within the next year), heatmap colours as appetite, and who owns the results and action plans (first line owns, second or third line tracks).

selectors.name: KRIs versus KPIs and KCIs
selectors.what: Distinguishing key risk indicators (signal a rise or fall in the likelihood or impact of a risk), key performance indicators (performance) and key control indicators (control effectiveness in design or performance), including how they overlap and how thresholds express appetite.

selectors.name: Loss-data collection criteria and boundaries
selectors.what: Regulatory criteria for operational loss data (10 years of data, minimum threshold EUR 20,000, mapping to Basel event types, dates, independent review), standard fields and net loss = gross loss - recoveries, the four dates, direct versus indirect losses, grouped losses, credit and market boundary events, and completeness checks.

notSelected: ORR-3 (top-down and bottom-up identification, extreme risk identification, taxonomies: taxonomies are A22), ORR-4 d to g (factor models, fault tree, Swiss cheese, bowtie, capital approaches, operational resilience), ORR-5 a and d to g (risk responses, human error and process quality, new initiatives and M&A, limiting impact, transfer and reputation) and ORR-6 a to d (reporting audiences, content, challenges, external reporting) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
